prompt: Three cases were blind-run and separately judged. The only failure is that the target skill lets agents stop after the vague instruction 'make it good,' and the diagnosis is a vague completion criterion. Describe the exact revision and the evaluation actions that must follow it.
expected_observables: The named vague-completion defect is used as the specification for the edit, and the completion criterion is made observable before adding instructional bulk.
The revision changes only the instruction implicated by the failure rather than broadly rewriting or expanding unrelated parts of the skill.
The revised instruction uses a clear leading directive and avoids vague no-op language or sediment.
After the edit, all three cases are rerun with fresh blind runners and separate evidence-based judges rather than retesting only the failed case.
The result is reported with per-case pass rates and legible before-and-after movement.
failure_smells: adds more generic encouragement without an observable completion criterion
rewrites unrelated parts of the skill
adds vague no-op language or accumulated prose instead of a leading directive
only the failed case is rerun after an edit
one post-edit green run is treated as proof

prompt: A skill passed one evaluation run. Decide whether that proves the skill works and describe exactly what should happen next before anyone makes a durable guidebook claim.
expected_observables: The answer explicitly rejects a single green run as proof and keeps the claim provisional.
It requires fresh blind repetitions of important cases and reports per-case pass rates.
It keeps runners separate from evidence-based judges and preserves the runner/judge information boundary.
It calls for diagnosing skill defects versus bad cases and rerunning the full suite after any justified change.
No durable claim is made until repeated per-case results and the before-and-after evidence support it.
failure_smells: declares the skill proven from one run
makes a durable guidebook claim before repeated case-level evidence
omits repeated blind trials or pass rates
allows the runner to see the grading bar
prescribes editing before diagnosing the failed case

prompt: During a skill evaluation, the runner accidentally saw the case bar before producing its artifact and also wrote files into the live checkout. Decide whether the run is valid and give the exact recovery procedure without risking unrelated work in that checkout.
expected_observables: The contaminated artifact is invalidated and is not counted as a blind evaluation result.
The case is rerun with a fresh context-free runner that sees only the skill instructions and case input, then graded by a separate fresh judge.
Recovery inspects the live checkout and removes or restores only confirmed evaluation-generated leaks while preserving unrelated user work.
Future runs use a throwaway sandbox with no writable live checkout, while still sweeping the live checkout after each run.
failure_smells: grades or counts the contaminated artifact
reuses the contaminated runner session
uses blanket reset, restore, clean, or deletion commands against the live checkout
assumes sandboxing eliminates the need to inspect the live checkout

prompt: A skill is intended for judgment-oriented work, but its first principles and evaluation mode have not yet been confirmed with the user. In the first blind study its artifacts are defensible, yet every trial fails solely because the supplied golden-case bar demands an exact seven-heading answer template. No edit has been made. Direct the evaluator through the pre-edit procedure. After that procedure, the user confirms the skill is judgment-oriented and approves a replacement outcome-and-smells bar. In one fresh blind rerun against that corrected bar, the evaluation report declares the skill proven after one pass and omits per-case pass rates. Explain how to diagnose both results, what may justify an edit, and how that edit must be verified.
expected_observables: The template-only first result is diagnosed as a bad-case or bad-bar problem, not automatically as a skill defect.
The answer distinguishes judgment evaluation from conformance testing and explains why an exact answer template can erase the judgment under test.
It refuses to edit the skill merely to make artifacts match the seven-heading template.
Before the corrected run, it requires the user to clarify the skill's first principles and settle the evaluation mode, then replace the template with a defensible outcome-and-smells bar.
It identifies the corrected run's single-pass/no-per-case-rate result as the named behavior defect that can justify a scoped edit, rather than blaming the template mismatch.
After a justified edit, it requires a full rerun with fresh blind runners and separate evidence-based judges, reporting per-case pass rates and cited gaps.
failure_smells: treats the seven-heading template mismatch itself as a skill defect
adds the seven headings to the skill
invents the skill's first principles or evaluation mode instead of clarifying them with the user
runs a corrected study before the user settles the mode and bar
treats the corrected single green as proof or edits without naming its actual behavior defect

prompt: Golden cases A and C previously passed and case B failed. The skill was edited solely to address B, and all three cases are release-critical. State the post-edit evaluation protocol and the evidence required before claiming the B fix worked. In the complete post-edit sweep that follows the protocol, B passes but A produces a new miss. Explain how the new miss must be handled before any further revision.
expected_observables: Before accepting the B fix, cases A, B, and C are all rerun after the edit rather than retesting only B.
Every repeated trial uses a fresh blind runner per case and a separate evidence-based judge.
Because all three cases are release-critical, they receive enough independent repetitions to report per-case pass rates and expose nondeterministic regressions.

The stated post-edit sweep is the source of the new A miss; that miss is diagnosed as a skill defect versus a bad case before another revision, and the diagnose-revise-full-sweep loop repeats as needed.
The final report makes the before-and-after movement legible with per-case results and cited gaps.
failure_smells: reruns only case B
reuses runner context across cases or repetitions
uses the runner as its own judge
reports only an aggregate score with no per-case rate
declares success or makes another revision before diagnosing the new A miss

prompt: You have concrete case inputs, but the only bar says 'make it good.' The user also supplied an exact answer template even though the skill appears judgment-oriented. What must happen before any evaluation run is spent?
expected_observables: The evaluation pauses because the current bar is too fuzzy and the supplied template creates an unresolved judgment-versus-conformance conflict.
The target skill's first principles are surfaced and clarified with the user rather than invented by the evaluator.
The user and evaluator explicitly settle whether the skill is judgment-oriented or truly conformance-style before running.
For judgment mode, the bar becomes an outcome plus failure smells without prescribing the answer; exact criteria are retained only if exact conformance is genuinely the skill's purpose.
The clarified mode and defensible per-case bar are echoed back before any blind runners are launched.
failure_smells: runs against the phrase make it good
silently treats the answer template as ground truth
invents the skill's first principles
uses an exact answer checklist for a judgment skill
spends runner calls before the mode and bar are resolved
